column1: # AUDIT: formal.lean.normalize / formal.normalize, at the three pins and on master.
# QUESTION (ledger section 6.4 step 3 makes the option set load-bearing): does the
# pins' `normalize=true` match an existing master route, is the flag simply no
# longer exposed, or was a preprocessing BEHAVIOUR removed?
# ANSWER, from the sources and the history, not from the names:
#   `normalize` is a WRITE-ONLY member of the Lean pass at ALL THREE PINS.  It is
#   declared, parsed and registered, and READ NOWHERE.  `if (normalize)` does not
#   occur anywhere in pass/lean at any pin -- and `git log -S'if (normalize)' --
#   pass/lean` returns NO commit in master's entire history either, so the Lean
#   emitter never read it at any point.
#   The behaviour the NAME refers to is real, but it lives in the ISABELLE
#   emitter and is PRESERVED on master: `if (ctx.normalize)
#   normalize_zero_width_get_masks(ctx, topo);`.
#   So: no preprocessing behaviour was removed from the Lean route, because there
#   never was one behind this flag on the Lean route.  A mis-used flag is simply
#   no longer exposed there.  This is NOT a no-op option added to make the sets
#   match, and no legacy normalization was restored.
#   Master's `check_labels` (pass/common/eprp_method.cpp:15-28) enforces only
#   REQUIRED labels, so passing `--set formal.lean.normalize=true` to master is
#   accepted and ignored -- no error and, since neither side ever read it, no
#   difference in emitted bytes.
#   ATTRIBUTION: the removal is UPSTREAM, not this port.  b7a24e0b0, Jose Renau,
#   2026-09-14, "several cleanups and reviews on options and miss-used options",
#   295 commits back on master; it is present in the D3/D4 repos but is NOT an
#   ancestor of their pins, and is absent from the FP repo entirely.
